title_en: Some users claim Claude is silently sabotaging projects, but the behavior may stem from a clash between its proactive nature and strict instruction following (Drew Breunig)
author: Drew Breunig
content_snippet:

The discussion around this is interesting for a few reasons.

The model that underlies Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 is a step forward in general capabilities. title_en: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secret theft and alleged coercion of shared suppliers
author: Matthias Bastian
content_snippet:

OpenAI accuses Apple of "coercing and threatening"suppliers that work with both companies and of using its market power to stifle competition.

summary_en: OpenAI has filed a countersuit against Apple in a California court, accusing the company of unfair business practices, including coercing shared suppliers and abusing its market power. title: Verizon in talks over $6bn deal for Fidium to boost broadband footprint
title_en: Verizon in talks over $6bn deal for Fidium to boost broadband footprint
author: Oliver Barnes, Sujeet Indap, and Kieran Smith
content_snippet:
US telecoms company Verizon is in talks over a roughly $6bn deal to buy fibre-optic broadband operator Fidium in a potential boost to its goal of making its network available to as many as 50mn homes and businesses nationwide.

The potential acquisition would come on the heels of the completion of Verizon’s $20bn takeover of Frontier Communications earlier this year, which added 2.2mn fibre-optic subscribers across 25 US states and expanded its network to reach an additional 9mn premises.

Offer
summary_en: Verizon is in advanced talks to acquire fiber-optic broadband operator Fidium for approximately $6 billion. The acquisition aims to scale Verizon's fiber infrastructure, enhancing its ability to bundle fixed-broadband and mobile services to improve customer retention and drive revenue growth.

title: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
title_en: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
author: Matthias Bastian
content_snippet:
It's no surprise at this point, but for the record: Two Chinese companies installed Nvidia's powerful Blackwell chips at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, who had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The details come from documents filed with Chinese regulators and reviewed by Bloomberg.

According to the filings, Shanghai Shuoyao offered a GB300-NVL72 rack as collateral for a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, while a second company, Shanghai Kezhan
summary_en: Shanghai Shuoyao and Shanghai Kezhan listed Nvidia GB300-NVL72 racks and GB200 servers as loan collateral in filings with Shanghai Innovation Bank. The hardware traces back to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte, and Shanghai Shuoyao maintains deep business ties with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm recently added to the US trade blacklist.
title_zh: 禁售英伟达芯片现身上海数据中心
summary_zh: 上海数据中心违规部署英伟达GB200/GB300服务器，该中心关联至遭美方制裁的芯片贸易链条

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 上海硕瑶与上海克展两家公司在向上海创新银行申请贷款的抵押物清单中，明确列出了英伟达GB300-NVL72机柜及GB200服务器。经查，相关硬件设备溯源指向台湾制造厂商技嘉科技，且上海硕瑶与此前被美方列入贸易黑名单的新加坡企业Megaspeed存在深度业务关联。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Shanghai Shuoyao and Shanghai Kezhan listed Nvidia GB300-NVL72 racks and GB200 servers as loan collateral in filings with Shanghai Innovation Bank. The hardware traces back to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte, and Shanghai Shuoyao maintains deep business ties with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm recently added to the US trade blacklist.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】上海硕瑶、上海克展、Megaspeed（涉事企业）、英伟达（芯片供应商）、技嘉科技（硬件制造）在上海某数据中心：违规安装并抵押禁售级AI加速芯片GB200/GB300系列
【起因与机理】绕过美方针对高端算力芯片的对华出口管制措施
【关键技术规格】企业利用禁售芯片作为银行贷款抵押物，暴露了算力资产的违规流通路径。
【各方立场与态度】通过序列号溯源确定设备源自台湾技嘉科技，引发出口合规审计压力升级。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Shanghai Shuoyao, Shanghai Kezhan, Megaspeed, Nvidia, Gigabyte (A Shanghai-based data center): Illegal deployment and collateralization of sanctioned Blackwell-series chips
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Circumvention of US export control regulations on high-end AI compute
[Regulatory & Investigation Focus] Use of sanctioned chips as collateral exposes illicit hardware circulation paths.
[Key Position & Outlook] Hardware serial numbers trace back to Gigabyte, raising pressure on export compliance.

Europe is falling behind the US on AI use at work, and the main reason is not technology, according to a new report.The report from Sifted, sponsored by London Business School, says Europe has an organisational gap rather than a tech gap. Firms struggle with skills, management, trust and the cost of fitting AI into how they work.

“Doing a fun thing with ChatGPT and running your whole business on AI are two very different things,” Celonis executive Rupal Karia told Sifted.

summary_en: A report by the European Central Bank and London Business School reveals that while technical potential exists, only 20% of EU firms have adopted AI, compared to 43% of US employees. European organizations are struggling with management adaptation, skill gaps, and unclear ROI, resulting in a 'tools without use-cases' adoption crisis.

title: Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models
title_en: Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models
author: Maximilian Schreiner
content_snippet:
AI pioneer Yann LeCun doesn't believe language models alone will lead to human-like intelligence. With his JEPA architecture, he is pursuing machines that model cause and effect and plan their actions in advance. Three new studies show how the pieces of this project fit together and where physics still sets limits.

In late 2025, Yann LeCun left Meta after shaping its AI research for 12 years. He cited the company's growing focus on large language models as one reason, then co-founded the Paris
summary_en: AI scientist Yann LeCun left Meta in late 2025 to co-found AMI Labs. The company is advancing the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to model cause-and-effect in physical environments, aiming to transcend the limitations of current Large Language Models in physical world interaction.

author: Reed Albergotti
content_snippet:

summary_en: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should target only the most advanced technology rather than a total blockade. He warned that over-restricting China forces domestic acceleration in chip development, whereas maintaining a 'generation gap' via older equipment exports keeps Beijing tethered to Western hardware ecosystems.

summary_en: Dragos Chief Research Officer HD Moore revealed that AI startup MiniMax improperly stores private web links from user prompts despite opt-out requests. ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软揭露中国与朝鲜背景的黑客组织（包括Salt Typhoon等）已将AI驱动的渗透测试平台ARTEX集成至攻击套件中。该工具通过自动化侦察、凭据攻击及漏洞扫描，将攻击周期缩短至分钟级，并能通过行为混淆绕过签名检测。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Microsoft reports that state-sponsored hacking groups, including Salt Typhoon, have integrated the AI-powered penetration testing tool ARTEX into their offensive arsenals. By automating reconnaissance, credential theft, and vulnerability scanning, the tool compresses intrusion cycles to minutes while bypassing static signature detection via behavioral obfuscation.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】微软安全情报部门、Salt Typhoon、Crystal Typhoon等攻击组织在全球关键基础设施与电信领域：利用AI平台ARTEX实施自动化网络侦察与提权入侵
【起因与机理】AI技术的自动化特性可显著提升渗透效率并降低被传统防御系统监测的概率
【核心事实细节】ARTEX平台实现多阶段攻击的自动化，大幅缩短入侵时间。
【各方立场与态度】行为特征分析成为防御此类AI驱动型攻击的唯一可靠防线。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Microsoft Security Intelligence, Salt Typhoon, Crystal Typhoon: Utilization of the AI platform ARTEX for automated network reconnaissance and privileged access
[Root Cause & Mechanism] AI-enabled automation significantly accelerates intrusion timelines and evades traditional signature-based detection
[Key Fact Detail] ARTEX enables multi-stage automated attacks, significantly compressing intrusion cycles.
[Key Position & Outlook] Behavioral analysis emerges as the only viable defense against AI-driven intrusion.

summary_en: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia to comply with new US export control regulations. title: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals.
title_en: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals.
author: Josh Boswell
content_snippet:
Nvidia is selling its most cutting-edge chips to at least two companies that are U.S.-based, but are actually controlled by Chinese-owned firms, raising fresh questions about efforts to keep sensitive technology away from the nation's rivals, a CBS News investigation found.

One of the chip giant's "preferred partners" is a California company owned by a Chinese firm whose chief executive is a graduate of a Chinese military university, records show. Another California company was renamed after it
summary_en: Investigations reveal that several California-based NVIDIA partners are effectively controlled by Chinese firms, with executives linked to Chinese military institutions and blacklisted entities. These entities leverage their U.S. registration to procure high-end AI chips and circumvent export controls by rerouting hardware to China via third-party jurisdictions.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 多项调查证实，部分位于加利福尼亚州的NVIDIA授权合作伙伴实际受中国资本控制，其高管背景关联中国军事院校及被列入贸易黑名单的实体。这些主体利用美国注册身份获取高端AI芯片，并通过东南亚等第三方渠道规避出口管制，向中国境内输送算力资源。

These entities leverage their U.S. registration to procure high-end AI chips and circumvent export controls by rerouting hardware to China via third-party jurisdictions.

【起因与机理】地缘政治竞争背景下，中国对高算力硬件的刚需与美国技术封锁政策的博弈
【关键数据与实测】The company's U.S. revenue fell from $201 million to $4.7 million this year.。

title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
title_en: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
author: Emma Roth
content_snippet:
Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland ruled in favor of the CPSC, which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods, not a logistics provider, making it responsible for carrying out recalls of third-party products.

Amazon sued the CPSC in March 2025 after the agency ordered Amazon to recall over 400,000 “Fulfilled by Amazon” p
summary_en: The U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland ruled that Amazon acts as a distributor, not merely a logistics provider, regarding its 'Fulfilled by Amazon' services. Consequently, the company is mandated to comply with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's order to recall over 400,000 hazardous third-party products, including faulty carbon monoxide detectors and non-compliant children's apparel.

Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said.
